Author: @kaseywahl
Content:
Right before the crytpo crash in 2021, a friend of mine got really into blockchain development on the Solana blockchain. I was a "web 2" developer at the time, and he encouraged me to attend a Solana Hacker House event in Miami. I hadn't seen him in years, and he lives in Berlin, so I decided to go check  it out to see my buddy and check out what all the hype was about.

Not gonna lie: it was the cultiest thing I think I've ever been a part of since my baptism in an evangelical church as a kid. It was one of those events where, if you weren't absolutely drinking up whatever they were serving, you were being a hater, and raising legitimate concerns about security, saving large sums of coins to wallets that could only be retrieved with a password that you store on a slip of paper, or the ethics of NFT collections, DeFi, pump and dump schemes, etc, would be met with "not everyone's gonna get it" or "this is the future of finance! Get on board!" 

I left that event feeling utterly stupefied. I'd learned so much, and yet nothing at all.
Needless to say, I decided to build indie (not blockchain) games instead. Much happier.
